description.p: CrossFX processes everything the machine plays — a ten-band equalizer plus fidelity, ambience, surround, dynamic boost and bass — by presenting itself to PipeWire as a virtual sink that applications play into and forwarding the processed result to the real device. A second lane does the same for a microphone: denoising, a high-pass, an expander, the equalizer, a de-esser, a compressor and a limiter, published as a virtual source.

It is a native port of FxSound, FxSound LLC's audio enhancer for Windows, written in Rust with egui. The DSP is ported line by line from the original with some of its defects fixed, so a preset voiced in the original sounds slightly different here; for its factory and bonus presets it keeps the original's preset files unchanged. A running instance can be driven from the command line, over D-Bus and from compositor keybindings.

«Like FxSound for Windows», a new Experimental setting, brings back the Windows window, command line and tray, and at its last position the Windows sound. The power button no longer clicks in the applications it moves, and an optional WirePlumber script fades an application moved to another device instead of letting it click.

The microphone gets a lane of its own beside the speakers', with noise suppression at three levels, an adaptive de-esser, de-reverb, echo cancellation and a calibration wizard. Applications can keep a preset of their own, a running instance answers on D-Bus and reports its changes as they happen, and defects of the original DSP are fixed.
